report.headline: Not post-quantum
report.cause: TLS 1.3 works, but when offered X25519MLKEM768 the server asks for X25519 instead. Its TLS library doesn't have ML-KEM, or the groups are limited in config.

fixes.title: Upgrade the TLS library under the server
fixes.detail: Hybrid PQ (X25519MLKEM768) ships in OpenSSL 3.5+, current BoringSSL and AWS-LC, Go 1.24+ and rustls with aws-lc-rs. If curves are set by hand, add X25519MLKEM768 to the front of the list.
fixes.snippet:
# Go
cfg.CurvePreferences = nil // Go 1.24+ default includes X25519MLKEM768
# OpenSSL-based
Groups = X25519MLKEM768:X25519:prime256v1

fixes.title: Can't upgrade? Cloudflare Tunnel
fixes.detail: Run cloudflared next to the server. The tunnel from the server to Cloudflare already uses post-quantum key agreement, so the hop that leaves your network is protected even if the server isn't.

auth.headline: No ML-DSA certificate
auth.detail: Leaf: ec-p256 key, signed ecdsa-sha256. Listing ML-DSA schemes doesn't break it, and offered only ML-DSA it refuses cleanly — what any correct TLS stack does, so this doesn't show whether its stack could serve ML-DSA. The chain is 2744 bytes.

fixes.title: Add an ML-DSA-44 certificate next to the current one
fixes.detail: Serving ML-DSA needs a TLS library that has it (OpenSSL 3.5+) and an ML-DSA certificate. Configure it as a second certificate and key (dual certificates): the server picks per client, so today's clients keep the classical one. Cloudflare accepts ML-DSA certificates on the Cloudflare → origin hop; browsers don't take ML-DSA certificates from public CAs yet, so issue it from your own or an origin CA.

advice: Even ML-DSA-44 throughout won't fit TCP's initial window: plan for an ML-DSA leaf under a classical CA first (scenario 1), and watch Merkle Tree Certificates and trust-anchor negotiation (IETF drafts), which take most of the chain off the wire.
Certificate compression (RFC 8879) barely helps ML-DSA: its keys and signatures are random-looking bytes. It helps the names and extensions only.
